problem:
The depth $D,$ in meters, of a plant’s root system after $t$ months is modeled by $D(t)=\frac{1}{4}\sqrt{2t+13}.$ What is the instantaneous rate of change of the root depth when $t=6$ months?

The instantaneous rate of change when $t=6$ months is
{{field-1}} meters per month.

activity_context.topic_title: Rates of Change in Applied Contexts

feedback.problem:
Air is pumped into and released from a pressurized chamber. After $t$ minutes, the volume of air (in cubic meters) is modeled by

$$
A(t)=-6{t}^{2}+90t+400,\,0\le t\le 15.
$$

Find the exact value of the instantaneous rate of change of the air volume with respect to time when $t=7$ minutes.

The instantaneous rate of change when $t=7$ minutes is
{{field-1}} cubic meters per minute.
feedback.worked_solution:
The instantaneous rate of change of the air volume at $t=7$ minutes is ${A}^{′}(7).$

First, we take the derivative and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{′}(t) & =\frac{d}{dt}\,(-6{t}^{2}+90t+400) \\  & =-12t+90.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting $t=7,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{′}(7) & =-12(7)+90 \\  & =-84+90 \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the instantaneous rate of change of the air volume at $t=7$ minutes is $6$ cubic meters per minute.
